question: What is the primary purpose of a rectal washout in clinical practice?

options.A: To inflate the large intestine for a diagnostic X-ray image
options.B: To measure the exact core body temperature of the patient
options.C: To deliver systemic medications directly into the bloodstream
options.D: To thoroughly flush out the lower bowel and remove impacted stool

explanation: A rectal washout uses fluid to clean and clear out accumulated waste or meconium from the lower colon. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h1)

question: Why is a rectal washout commonly performed in neonates with Hirschsprung's disease?

options.A: To close an abnormal opening in the abdominal wall
options.B: To permanently cure the underlying genetic bowel defect
options.C: To clear impacted meconium caused by a lack of nerve cells
options.D: To stimulate rapid weight gain and improve infant nutrition

explanation: The absence of ganglion cells stops normal movement, requiring a washout to remove trapped meconium. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h1)

question: A neonatal condition that frequently requires a rectal washout is...
explanation: Newborns with meconium plug syndrome cannot pass their first stool easily, making a washout necessary. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h2)

question: When is a rectal washout preferred over an oral bowel preparation?

options.A: When the patient requires complete cleansing of the entire small intestine
options.B: When the patient is fully conscious and eager to drink large volumes
options.C: When there is an active and severe infection in the stomach
options.D: When the patient cannot safely take medications or fluids by mouth

explanation: Rectal washouts bypass the upper gastrointestinal tract, making them ideal for patients unable to tolerate oral preparations. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h2)

question: Which condition represents an absolute contraindication for a rectal washout?
explanation: Introducing fluid into a perforated bowel pushes contents into the abdomen, causing severe infection. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h3)

question: What is the best patient position for performing a rectal washout?
explanation: The left lateral position follows the natural curve of the lower bowel for easier fluid entry. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h4)

question: Why must the washout fluid be warmed to body temperature before use?

options.A: To speed up the chemical dissolution of hard fecal masses
options.B: To ensure the fluid remains sterile inside the irrigation bag
options.C: To prevent abdominal cramping caused by cold temperature shock
options.D: To kill any bacteria present in the normal saline solution

explanation: Cold fluid triggers reflex bowel spasms and pain, making the procedure difficult to tolerate. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h4)

question: What type of lubricant should always be used on the catheter tip?
explanation: Water-soluble gels protect delicate mucosal tissues and dissolve easily without harming the bowel. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h5)

question: What should the nurse do immediately if resistance is felt while advancing the catheter?

options.A: Quickly infuse a large volume of fluid to clear the block
options.B: Rotate the catheter rapidly to break up the resistance
options.C: Apply gentle physical force to push past the obstruction
options.D: Stop advancing immediately and investigate the cause

explanation: Forcing a catheter against resistance can easily cause a traumatic tear or bowel perforation. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h5)

question: What critical calculation must be performed during and after a rectal washout?

options.A: Body mass index and surface area
options.D: Fluid balance of input versus output

explanation: Tracking fluid in and out ensures the patient is not retaining excessive fluid, which causes water intoxication. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h6)

question: Which symptom in a newborn after a washout suggests possible vagal nerve overstimulation?
explanation: Rectal manipulation can stimulate the vagus nerve, causing a drop in heart rate and pale, clammy skin. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h6)

question: Which detail is NOT necessary to include in the rectal washout documentation?

options.A: The patient's tolerance of the procedure
options.B: The total volume of fluid instilled
options.C: The color and consistency of effluent
options.D: The brand name of the lubricant used

explanation: Specific commercial brand names of routine supplies are clinically irrelevant for charting patient outcomes. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h7)

question: What is the primary legal and professional reason for documenting nursing care accurately?

options.A: It allows the billing department to charge extra fees for specialized equipment
options.B: It prevents the hospital from ever facing patient complaints or lawsuits
options.C: It guarantees that the patient will recover faster from the primary illness
options.D: It creates a reliable legal record that care was safely and correctly provided

explanation: Medical records serve as legal proof of the nursing interventions performed and the patient's response. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h7)
